title: IF/SWITCH inside iterator expression — callback risk
description: IF or SWITCH in the expression argument of an iterator (SUMX, AVERAGEX, …) is usually evaluated row by row by the Formula Engine (CallbackDataID in the storage-engine query). IF.EAGER, or moving the branch outside the iterator, lets the engine push the calculation down. Confirm with a query plan before rewriting — simple branches are sometimes optimised. Iterating a reduced grain (VALUES / DISTINCT / SUMMARIZE / a VAR table) is the canon's remedy and is reported at info only.
fix_suggestion: Use IF.EAGER when both branches are cheap, compute the condition once in a VAR outside the iterator, or split the iterator by the condition with CALCULATE.

title: IFERROR/ISERROR inside iterator — callback risk
description: IFERROR or ISERROR in the expression argument of an iterator forces step-by-step error checking for every row, completely preventing SE optimization. Import-mode advice: in DirectQuery IFERROR folds into the SQL and DIVIDE does not.
fix_suggestion: Handle the error condition explicitly before the iterator, or use DIVIDE for division errors

title: Nested iterators — O(n*m) callback risk
description: An iterator inside another iterator (e.g., SUMX inside SUMX) creates O(n*m) row-by-row evaluation. This scales quadratically with table size.
fix_suggestion: Flatten with SUMMARIZECOLUMNS, or use CALCULATE to avoid the inner iteration

title: FILTER over a whole model table with a single-column predicate
description: FILTER(Table, <predicate on one column>) iterates the expanded table. A column filter (CALCULATE(<expr>, KEEPFILTERS(Table[Col] = x)) or FILTER(VALUES(Table[Col]), …)) scans only that column. Filtering a table variable or a table expression is not flagged.
fix_suggestion: Filter the column instead of the table: KEEPFILTERS(Table[Col] = value) as a CALCULATE filter argument, or FILTER(VALUES(Table[Col]), …).

title: FORMAT returns text — breaks sorting/aggregation, callbacks inside iterators
description: FORMAT converts a value to text. In a measure body this breaks numeric sorting and aggregation (use the Format String / dynamic format string instead); inside an iterator it is evaluated row by row by the Formula Engine. Label / SVG measures that must build text are a legitimate use — suppress with `// lint-disable CB005`.
fix_suggestion: Use the measure's FormatString property or report-level formatting instead

title: LASTDATE in a scalar comparison — prefer MAX
description: In a scalar comparison, LASTDATE returns a single-row table where MAX returns a plain scalar date — simpler and more predictable. Note: as a CALCULATE filter argument (e.g. semi-additive CALCULATE([Balance], LASTDATE('Date'[Date]))) LASTDATE is the CORRECT choice and is not flagged here.
fix_suggestion: When comparing a date scalar, use MAX(DateColumn) instead of LASTDATE(DateColumn). Keep LASTDATE when it is a CALCULATE filter argument (semi-additive measures).

title: DIVIDE inside iterator expression
description: DIVIDE in an iterator expression can prevent storage-engine push-down of the division. Only when the denominator can never be 0 or BLANK (e.g. rows are pre-filtered with Table[Den] <> 0) is the / operator the faster, equivalent choice; otherwise DIVIDE is correct and should stay.
fix_suggestion: If the denominator is provably non-zero: CALCULATE(SUMX(T, T[A] / T[B]), T[B] <> 0). Otherwise keep DIVIDE.

title: Rounding function inside iterator expression
description: ROUND / ROUNDUP / ROUNDDOWN / CEILING / FLOOR / MROUND inside an iterator over fact rows are evaluated row by row by the Formula Engine (CallbackDataID; SQLBI measured 263x SE CPU on 200M rows). INT / TRUNC are SE-native and the canon's own remedy for IF (INT(col > 0) * x) - they are not flagged. Iterating the distinct values (VALUES / SUMMARIZE / ALL(col) / a VAR) is the remedy and is reported at info only.
fix_suggestion: Iterate the distinct values being rounded instead of every row: SUMX(SUMMARIZE(T, T[Price]), CALCULATE(SUM(T[Qty])) * ROUND(T[Price], 2)).

title: String function inside iterator expression
description: Text functions (LEFT, RIGHT, MID, SUBSTITUTE, REPLACE, CONCATENATE, UPPER, LOWER, TRIM, LEN, FIND, SEARCH, CONTAINSSTRING, REPT) inside an iterator over fact rows force row-by-row Formula Engine evaluation (a non-ASCII column additionally disables the bitmap text index - AP-12). Iterating the distinct values is reported at info only.
fix_suggestion: Move the string logic to a calculated column (or Power Query), or compute it once in a VAR outside the iterator.

title: SELECTEDVALUE / HASONEVALUE inside iterator expression
description: SELECTEDVALUE / HASONEVALUE inside an iterator is re-evaluated per row although it usually returns the same value for the whole iteration.
fix_suggestion: Cache it in a VAR before the iterator: VAR _sel = SELECTEDVALUE(T[C]) RETURN SUMX(T, … _sel …).

title: Time-intelligence function inside iterator expression
description: DATEADD / DATESYTD / DATESQTD / DATESMTD / DATESBETWEEN / DATESINPERIOD / SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR / PARALLELPERIOD inside an iterator build a new date filter per row.
fix_suggestion: Compute the date table once in a VAR before the iterator: VAR _dates = DATEADD(…) RETURN SUMX(T, CALCULATE([M], _dates)).
